title: Sh-U-V
hook: teshuvah, from the root to turn or return

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sh-B-T: the root of Shabbat, and of the manna that ceased. Your line was to stop. Did you manage one full minute? Day one thousand three hundred sixty-seven.

Three widows stand on a road leading out of Moab. Naomi is heading home to Bethlehem, and she tells her two daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' houses. "Turn again, my daughters," she says. Orpah kisses her and turns back. Ruth won't. She goes on with Naomi. And then the chapter ends with a strange line. It says Naomi returned, and Ruth with her, "which returned out of the country of Moab." Ruth returned. To a place she had never been. The verb doing all that turning and returning is today's root.
screen: `THREE WIDOWS ON A ROAD.` → `ORPAH TURNS BACK.` → `RUTH RETURNS, SOMEWHERE NEW.`

segments.voice: Sh-U-V. Shin, vav, vet. To turn, to return. From it comes teshuvah, the word often translated repentance. Turn it four ways. First, Ruth. The first chapter of Ruth keeps coming back to this verb: turn back, return. And it lets Ruth return to a land she's never seen. So teshuvah isn't only going back to where you were. It can be turning toward where you belong. Second, the prophet's call. Hosea says: "O Israel, return unto the LORD thy God." That verse is read on the Sabbath between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, and that Sabbath takes its name from it: Shabbat Shuvah, the Sabbath of Return. Third, both directions. The book of Lamentations ends with a plea: "Turn thou us unto thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old." Turn us, and we'll turn. The turning is asked for and done at the same time. Those words are sung in synagogue as the Torah scroll is returned to the ark. Fourth, how you know it's real. Maimonides, in his Laws of Teshuvah, asks what complete teshuvah looks like. His answer: the same situation comes around again, with the same pull, and the person, able to do the same thing, chooses differently. Not because the door is locked. Because they've turned. That's the root in one word: not a feeling of regret, but a change of direction you can see.
screen: `RUTH RETURNS TO A NEW PLACE.` · `SHABBAT SHUVAH.` · `TURN US, AND WE SHALL BE TURNED.` · `THE SAME CHOICE, CHOSEN DIFFERENTLY.` · then, large: `TURN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: turn back, once. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one small thing you've drifted from. A call you keep not making. A habit that slipped. A person you've been short with. Don't build a case against yourself. Just find the direction you've been facing, and the direction you'd rather face. Then, in your mind, make the turn. One step, one choice, the next time it comes around. Breathe into that new direction. If you pray, you can say the words from Lamentations, turn us, and we shall be turned. The bell holds the time.
Sh-U-V. Shin, vav, vet: to turn, to return. The root of teshuvah, the turning a person can choose. Today's word.
Your line: turn. Today, when the same old moment comes around, notice it, and choose the other direction, even once. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Teshuvah is a theme of the season from the month of Elul through Yom Kippur, and a blessing asking for return is also part of the weekday Amidah prayer.

they come from the end of Lamentations.

fork.setup: a year after you made a promise to change, the same situation comes back, with the same pull. you could do it again. what does Maimonides call complete teshuvah?
options: staying far away so it can't happen.
being able to do it, and choosing differently.
fork.reveal: in his Laws of Teshuvah, complete return is when the same chance comes and the person turns from it, not because they can't, but because they've changed.

original.note: Hebrew: return, repentance; from the root shin, vav, vet, to turn.

what a scholar hears: Ruth 1 uses the verb again and again, and has Ruth 'return' to a land she'd never seen; Maimonides tests teshuvah by the same choice made differently.
